newsitem.title: SOUTH AFRICA: Mobil Nigeria aims to cut gas flaring.
newsitem.headline: Mobil Nigeria aims to cut gas flaring.

text.p: Mobil Nigeria aims to cut back on the amount of gas it flares from its oil wells, production manager Victor Oyofo said on Tuesday.

Addressing the Africa Oil 1996 conference, Oyofo said that "by 1997 we hope we will have substantially reduced the gas that we flare because we are committed to ensuring near 100 percent full utilisation of gas".
He said that this would be done through using the gas for power generation and reinjection "so that there is very little left to be flared".
Flaring is burning off gas from oil wells rather than storing it, reinjecting it or shipping it ashore for commercial or industrial use.
Oyofo was reacting to criticism earlier on in the conference by senior World Bank oil and gas official Eric Daffern that African countries were flaring too much gas.
He said that the use of gas was extremely small in Africa.
"One area where Africa does stand out as a crying shame is the amount of flaring. Nigeria is at the top of the list but there are plenty of countries that flare extensively.
"We feel that it is quite important that that issue gets resolved. Flaring in the modern world is not the most appropriate way of going ahead."

Daffern said that Africa's extensive gas reserves were not being used because of the small markets available for gas but the World Bank was investigating ways in which it could be put to viable commercial use.
Some countries had already proved that gas could be used, without subsidisation, for projects such as power generation.
